ios.previous_incomplete_attempt: No root cause established; subsequent attached run with console logging completed all 12 cases without renderer changes.

conclusion: Metal reduces Flutter UI/raster work, but the current external texture path has substantially higher backend-request-to-raster-finish latency on both tested Apple devices. Same-sequence native iPhone input also has higher P95. Keep the existing mesh as default; do not migrate production on GPU time alone.
next_evidence: No production migration recommended. If pursuing Metal for more complex visual quality, inspect texture publication and Flutter frame scheduling first, measuring the complete path. Existing mesh first-drag tails remain a separate optimization target.
limitations: Raster finish is not display presentation or touch-to-photon latency.
Backend request timestamps do not cover identical framework work before request dispatch.
Clock matching rejects ambiguous copy/frame pairs; unobserved counts remain in paired report.
Output texture memory is a conservative five-buffer pool estimate; device allocation and process RSS include other subsystems.
No Apple Books visual parity claim; endpoint agreement does not establish intermediate-frame equivalence.
Paired app retains both backends; per-case RSS does not measure exclusive renderer memory.
Native input uses EPUB single page only; six-format/layout combinations use Flutter integration-test pointer events, not six native-input performance trials.
One native input run per backend; both have tail spikes. Maximum values 120.926 ms (mesh) and 83.213 ms (Metal) do not establish comparative cold-tail reliability.
